direct_claims: This chart is about winter temperature anomalies for the world, shown separately for December, January, and February.
It defines anomalies as the difference between each month's average surface temperature and the mean temperature of the same month during 1991–2020, measured in degrees Celsius.
The source attribution names Our World in Data and cites modified Copernicus Climate Change Service information for 2026.
In climate science, a temperature anomaly shows departure from a reference average rather than absolute temperature.
Because the baseline is 1991–2020, negative values mean that month was cooler than the recent climatological norm for that same month, and positive values mean it was warmer.
The three panels represent Northern Hemisphere winter months, and the note states that these correspond to opposite seasons in the Southern Hemisphere.
Exact rankings and values should be treated as approximate because only the image is available and the underlying metadata has been withheld.
